Answer questions about a text, an image or a recording with a decision model

Source: R/llm_verbs.R
decide.Rd

decide() sends a state (a text, a picture, a recording, a PDF or a mix) and a set of closed questions to a decision model and returns, for each question, the answer and the probability the model gives it. Use it to classify, screen or score texts and images where you want a calibrated number rather than free text. Give it many states at once and it runs the requests in parallel.

Usage

decide(
  .state,
  .questions,
  .provider = getOption("tidyllm_decide_default"),
  .dry_run = NULL,
  .timeout = NULL,
  .max_tries = NULL,
  .max_active = 5,
  .progress = FALSE
)

Arguments

.state

What to decide about. Every element is one item: a non-empty string, a media object, an LLMMessage, or a list of parts that belong together (one level only). Pass one item bare, a character vector, or a list of items; two or more items are decided in parallel. See the Many states section.

.questions

A tidyllm_schema() whose fields are the questions.

.provider

A provider call such as jev().

.dry_run

If TRUE, return the httr2 request without sending it (a list of requests, one per state, for many states).

.timeout

Timeout in seconds. Provider default if NULL.

.max_tries

Maximum attempts. Provider default if NULL.

.max_active

Most requests in flight at once when .state holds many states. The default is 5; a free Gemini key allows about 200 requests a minute, so lower it if you see rate-limit warnings.

.progress

Show a progress bar when .state holds many states.

Value

A tibble with one row per question and the columns question, type ("yes_no", "choice", "score" or "box"), answer ("yes" or "no", the chosen option, or the score level with the highest probability), probability (of that answer), confidence (the backend's confidence in the answer; for yes/no questions the larger of the probability of yes and of no when the backend gives none, and NA for choice and score questions) and probabilities (a list column with one named numeric vector over the options for each row). A box question gives one row with answer and probability NA, and the schema then also adds the numeric columns top, bottom, left and right (fractions of the image; NA on all other rows). For many states, one block of rows per state with state and state_id in front.

The attributes usage, latency and model describe the call. usage is a list with input_tokens and output_tokens (what the provider billed; NA when it does not report them), plus cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens for OpenAI and tokens_by_modality for Gemini. latency is the elapsed seconds. For many states, usage sums the states that succeeded, latency is the time of the whole parallel run, and model is the model the first reply names. With .dry_run = TRUE, the request.

Details

Questions are the fields of a tidyllm_schema(). field_lgl() is a yes/no question, field_fct(.levels = ) is a choice question, and field_fct(.levels = , .ordered = TRUE) is a score question over ordered levels. The field description is the question text. .level_descriptions in field_fct() tells the model what each option or level means; for a score question the level order is the scale. field_lgl(.true = , .false = ) defines what yes and no mean; give both or neither.

Media

A state can hold images, audio, video and PDFs next to text. A media object (img(), audio_file(), video_file(), pdf_file()) is an item, and so is an LLMMessage (the text of its last user message, then its media). To put several parts into one item, wrap them in a list inside .state: list(list(photo_a = img("a.jpg"), photo_b = img("b.jpg"))). Names inside the item label the parts, so a question can say "the animal in photo_a". The providers read:

ProviderReadsImage option
jev()imagenone
openai()image.detail
gemini()image, audio, video, PDF.resolution
ollama()image (not yet tested against a live server)none

provider_capabilities(.what = "decide_media") gives the same table as a tibble. A provider that cannot read a media type stops with a message before any request; decide() also checks image size, format and count against the provider's limits and never resizes an image. A PDF sent to a provider that does not read PDFs is replaced by its extracted text; a PDF made with pdf_file(.text_extract = TRUE) always goes as text. Either way decide() tells you once per call, naming the provider and the files, that layout, tables and figures are lost. A PDF without extractable text stops the call.

Images, audio and video leave your machine and go to the provider. Do not send restricted or personal data, such as survey photos with faces.

Many states

Every element of .state is one item. An item is a string, a media object, an LLMMessage, or a list of parts that belong together (strings and media objects, one level only; names label the parts). .state itself is one item passed bare, a character vector (one item per string), or a list of items (one item per element). So list(img("a.jpg"), img("b.jpg")) is two items, and list(list("Caption", img("c.jpg"))) is one item with two parts.

A single item, however it is given, returns the plain tibble. Two or more items give one result tibble with a leading state column (the item's name when the outer list is named, else its text cut to 60 characters or a short description of its media) and an integer state_id, then the usual columns.

The requests run in parallel, at most .max_active at a time, and are retried like a single request. A state that fails after its retries, or that the model refuses, gives NA rows and one warning; the other states are kept. A malformed item stops the call before any request and names its position.

Finding things in images (experimental)

field_box() asks where something is in an image and returns one box. Only jev() answers it; openai(), gemini() and ollama() stop with a message before any request, and so does a state without an image. A box question always returns a box, so pair it with a yes/no presence question. The vendor labels this as preview and the format may change. See field_box() and box_to_pixels().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
questions <- tidyllm_schema(
  late = field_lgl("Was the payment late?"),
  tone = field_fct("Tone of the message", .levels = c("polite", "angry")),
  severity = field_fct("How severe is the complaint?",
    .levels = c("low", "medium", "high"), .ordered = TRUE)
)
decide("The invoice arrived three weeks late and nobody answers my mails.",
       questions, jev())

# Many texts: one tibble with a state and state_id column
mails <- c("Payment is three weeks late.", "Thanks, all fine.")
decide(mails, questions, openai())

# An image, and two labelled images in one item
cat_q <- tidyllm_schema(cat = field_lgl("Is the animal in the picture a cat?"))
decide(img("cat.jpg"), cat_q, openai(.detail = "low"))
pets <- tidyllm_schema(
  a_dog = field_lgl("Is the animal in photo_a a dog?"),
  b_dog = field_lgl("Is the animal in photo_b a dog?")
)
decide(list(list(photo_a = img("cat.jpg"), photo_b = img("dog.jpg"))), pets, jev())

# Many images: one item per element
files <- c("cat.jpg", "dog.jpg")
decide(purrr::map(files, img), cat_q, gemini(.resolution = "low"))
} # }
